jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: My Biggest Fan
jokes.joke: I was walking through the park when a woman ran up to me and said, 'Oh my God, can I get a picture?' I said, 'Of course!' She handed me her phone and went back to stand with her husband. Apparently, I have the kind of face people trust with a $1,200 phone but don't want in a photograph.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Park Bench Red Flags
jokes.joke: I dated a guy for two months before I found out he was an assassin. Should've clocked it sooner -- every date was a walk in the park, and he'd pick the bench, survey the exits, then say 'perfect, nobody can see us here.' I thought he was romantic. He was doing recon. And when I finally broke up with him, he looked more nervous than I'd ever seen him on the job.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Grass Is Greener
jokes.joke: I’ve been trying to get into an exclusive country club for three years, and last week I finally got rejected for the fourth time. So I went to the public park to clear my head. Turns out it’s the exact same experience, except the guys yelling at me to hurry up are toddlers on tricycles, and the water hazard is just a guy washing his socks in the fountain. Honestly, the dress code is way more relaxed, and nobody’s judging my swing.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Tipped Assassin
jokes.joke: My coveted goal was always to become a successful assassin. I keep not achieving it. Last job, I had the perfect moment. The target looked right at me. I panicked and asked for directions to the nearest coffee shop. We walked there together. He paid. My handler said that was the first time a mark ever tipped the assassin.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Participation Bench
jokes.joke: I trained all year to run a marathon and finally crossed the finish line in the park. My buddy said, "You must feel amazing." I said, "Not really. My dream was to qualify for Boston." He goes, "How far off were you?" I said, "About three hundred miles south."
